# Dialing in the Open

[REDACTED]

This repository accompanies the ACM IMC 2026 paper "Dialing in the Open: A
Security Census of Internet-Facing Voice Infrastructure."

The repository contains the measurement code, analysis scripts, and
instructions for reproducing the reported results from the released artifact
data.

## Citation

The entry below is provisional. The DOI, page numbers, and final author
metadata will be added when ACM publishes the proceedings.

```bibtex

  author = {Vidur Gupta},
```

## Reproducing the results

The step-by-step reproduction guide is in `code/README.md`. It lists the
required files, commands, and expected results.

The normal reproduction path uses the archived artifact data. Do not rerun an
Internet-wide scan to reproduce the paper.

## Data release and vulnerable hosts

The public artifact does not publish raw scanned IP addresses or a list of
systems with inferred security weaknesses. Publishing those records could
make it easier to target systems that remain online.

The archival release instead provides privacy-preserving derived data and
aggregate results. It removes raw IP addresses, hostnames, SIP responses,
authentication nonces, certificate names that identify hosts, and other fields
that could reveal a vulnerable system. Any later record-level derived tables
will use opaque identifiers, and rare combinations will be aggregated when
they could identify an endpoint.

This approach preserves the inputs needed to check the paper's aggregate
results while reducing the risk of identifying individual systems. The raw
IP-level archive remains private. This is a partial data release for security
and privacy reasons, as permitted by the
[IMC 2026 artifact policy](https://conferences.sigcomm.org/imc/2026/cfp/).

### Release safety check

The release process examines every generated data record, not a sample. It
uses an allowlist of fields and fails if public data contain a globally
routable IP address, raw SIP message, authentication nonce, certificate
hostname, credential, or other direct host identifier. It also checks all
public text files for IP addresses and secret-like values. Groups that are
small enough to identify a system are suppressed or combined before release.

This validation is entirely offline. It reads the archived local data and does
not contact any measured host. The exact validation command will be included
in the step-by-step reproduction guide.

## Ethics and opt-out process

The application-layer probes identified the research landing page in their
`User-Agent`. During measurement, that page explained the project, provided a
contact route, and included a form for requesting exclusion. An exclusion list
was used for scanning and requests were honored.

The public artifact documents this process but does not include form
submissions, operator messages, names, email addresses, or other personal
contact information. The operations record does not contain a complete count
of opt-out requests, complaints, blocks, or inquiries, so the artifact does
not report an unverified count.

## Repository layout

```text
code/       Measurement and analysis code
data/       Privacy-preserving derived data and aggregate results
```

Internal review records, raw measurement data, credentials, and third-party
paper PDFs are not part of the public artifact.

## Network safety

The full measurement scripts can target the entire routable IPv4 address
space, which is roughly 3.7 billion addresses. Running them is not an ordinary
software test. Network operators may flag the traffic, send abuse reports, or
block the source. A cloud or Internet provider may suspend an account that
performs an unauthorized scan.

Do not run the scanning pipeline merely to reproduce the paper. The provided
reproduction workflow is offline and does not contact measured hosts.

Any new scan requires authorization from the network that originates the
traffic and compliance with the hosting provider's policies. It also requires
dedicated infrastructure, conservative rate limits, an exclusion list, a
public research-information page, a working contact and opt-out process, and
active monitoring for operator complaints. Test only on systems you own until
that process is complete.
